subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: The probability that a person chosen at random is left-handed (in handwriting) is 0.1. What is the probability that in a group of 10 people, there is one who is left-handed?

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability that one person in ten is left-handed — what n, p and q are, and which term of the binomial formula you use.
insider_note: The book reads this as EXACTLY one left-handed person, P(X = 1) = ¹⁰C₁ (9/10)⁹ (1/10), and the ¹⁰C₁ = 10 cancels the 1/10 to leave (9/10)⁹. The English also allows 'at least one', which would be 1 − (9/10)¹⁰ and a very different number — write which reading you are taking.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write n, p, q
steps.margin_note: First mark. Each person is one trial; success = left-handed, p = 0.1 = 1/10, q = 9/10; the group of 10 gives n = 10. Write all three before the formula.
steps.memory_tip: Each person is one trial: p = 0.1 = 1/10, q = 9/10, and the group of 10 gives n = 10.
lines: X is binomial with n = 10, p = 1/10.

recall.must_convey: That n = 10, p = 1/10 and q = 9/10, with X the number of left-handed people.
accept: n is ten, p is one by ten and q is nine by ten, X is the number of left handed people
each person is a trial with success probability point one, ten trials
p point one, q point nine, n ten
prathi person oka trial, p one by ten, q nine by ten, n ten
binomial with n ten and p one tenth

steps.why: Ten independent people with the same chance of being left-handed is a binomial situation. Naming n, p and q is what turns the word problem into the formula.
common_mistakes: Taking p = 0.9 as the success probability.

steps.label: Find P(X = 1)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. P(X = 1) = ¹⁰C₁ q⁹ p = 10 · (9/10)⁹ · (1/10). The 10 cancels the 1/10, leaving (9/10)⁹.
steps.memory_tip: The ¹⁰C₁ = 10 cancels the 1/10, leaving exactly (9/10)⁹. Say you read it as EXACTLY one.

accept: P of one is ten C one into nine by ten to the nine into one by ten which is nine by ten to the nine
ten times nine tenths to the ninth times one tenth, the tens cancel
the answer is nine by ten to the power nine
ten C one into nine by ten power nine into one by ten, ten cancel aithe nine by ten power nine
heard_as: nine by ten to the nine

steps.why: Exactly one success in ten trials is the r = 1 term. The binomial coefficient ¹⁰C₁ = 10 counts which of the ten people it is, and it cancels the single factor of p = 1/10.
common_mistakes: Writing (1/10)⁹ (9/10) — the powers on p and q swapped.
